d: The Strategic Bid and Pursuit Manager converts qualified business opportunities into client-informed, differentiated and commercially sound pursuit strategies. The role leads opportunity qualification, bid strategy, cross-functional coordination and submission governance from early engagement through award or loss, helping the business focus its resources on better-qualified and more winnable bids.

Working closely with Business Development and Estimation, the role translates client and market intelligence into clear direction for the wider bid team. Business Development retains ownership of the opportunity pipeline and client relationship, while Estimation retains responsibility for quantity take-offs, pricing build-up, estimate accuracy and estimating compliance.
q: Lead structured qualification reviews before significant estimating resources are committed.
Assess strategic fit, client credibility, scope clarity, competitive position, delivery capacity, programme, contractual and payment risks, and the credibility of the route to win.
Recommend bid, no-bid, conditional bid or monitor decisions, supported by clear rationale, conditions and required management actions.
Prioritise the pursuit portfolio according to strategic value, probability of success, resource demand and timing.
Prepare a concise bid strategy and kick-off brief covering client needs, win themes, competitors, differentiators, pricing posture, value engineering, risks, responsibilities and timetable.
Translate client and market intelligence into clear direction for Estimation and other contributors.
Coordinate inputs from Estimation, Commercial, Operations, Design/FDP, Procurement, Manufacturing, Quality and HSE.
Establish milestones, review gates, decision deadlines and content ownership, resolving gaps that may affect quality or timing.
Drive solutions that improve value, buildability, lead time, quality and commercial competitiveness without weakening compliance or delivery confidence.
Review tender requirements at a strategic level with the relevant technical and commercial owners.
Ensure material technical, contractual, commercial, programme, logistics, capacity, warranty, payment and interface risks are identified and addressed.
Challenge whether the proposed scope, solution, programme and commercial position align with client priorities and the company’s delivery capability.
Develop differentiated content, including execution methodology, manufacturing strategy, value-engineering options, procurement plans, quality controls and programme narratives.
Lead final readiness reviews and ensure the offer presents one coherent position across price, technical response, programme, exclusions, qualifications and presentation.
Coordinate tender interviews, clarification responses, best-and-final offers and negotiation support, escalating departures from approved margin, risk or delivery parameters.
Lead structured handovers covering strategy, assumptions, client commitments, risks, qualifications, value-engineering proposals and negotiation history.
Obtain feedback following a loss or withdrawal and conduct concise win/loss reviews.
Maintain reusable client, competitor, benchmark, case-study and bid-content intelligence.
Work with Estimation, Procurement and technical teams to strengthen value-engineering sources, outsourcing options and specialist partner networks.
Use evidence from pursuits to improve governance, estimating interfaces, bid content and management decision-making.
The ideal candidate for the role of Strategic Bid and Pursuit Manager has the following skills, personal qualities and experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Commercial Management or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

At least 10 years of relevant experience in bids, pre-construction, estimating, commercial management, business development or project delivery within interior fit-out, high-quality joinery, hospitality or specialist contracting.
Proven experience shaping and leading complex competitive bids, rather than only preparing estimates or administering tender submissions.
Strong understanding of fit-out and manufacturing interfaces, including design development, specialist packages, procurement, programme, logistics, quality and site delivery.
Sound commercial and contractual awareness, with the ability to identify risk and develop appropriate clarifications and qualifications.
Confidence in client discussions, tender interviews, negotiation support and cross-functional management reviews.
Strategic and commercially aware, with the ability to understand client priorities, decision criteria and credible sources of competitive advantage.
Influential and collaborative, with the ability to challenge assumptions and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
Evidence led and organised, with disciplined management of facts, assumptions, risks, decisions and commitments.
Delivery minded, balancing ambition with buildability, operational capacity, programme, risk and margin.
Clear written and spoken business English, with the ability to turn complex technical and commercial matters into concise decisions and persuasive bid narratives.
Working proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications; familiarity with CRM, opportunity-tracking, document-control or bid-management platforms is advantageous.
Experience in a multicultural GCC environment and Arabic or another relevant regional language are advantageous.
Professional integrity and commitment to confidentiality, realistic commitments and company procedures.
r: Partner with Business Development and management to identify priority opportunities where early engagement can strengthen the route to win.
Build credible relationships with clients, developers, operators, consultants, designers and project managers while respecting procurement and confidentiality requirements.
Develop opportunity intelligence covering client objectives, stakeholder expectations, design intent, quality, budget, programme, competitors, decision criteria and procurement route.
Position the company’s fit-out and manufacturing capabilities through targeted discussions, capability submissions, factory visits, workshops, samples, mock-ups and budget exercises.
Maintain clear records of client intelligence, assumptions, commitments and next actions.
